cards.claim: To solve an equation, the same mathematical operation is performed on both sides so that the balance between the sides is not disturbed.
cards.quote: We perform the same mathematical operations on both sides of the equation, so that the balance is not disturbed.

cards.claim: Subtracting a variable term such as x from both sides of an equation amounts to transposing that term to the other side.
cards.quote: Also, note that subtracting x from both sides amounts to transposing x to LHS.

locator.section: 2.2 Solving Equations having the Variable on both Sides

cards.claim: Like numbers, variable terms can be transposed from one side of an equation to the other.
cards.quote: Just as numbers, variables can, also, be transposed from one side of the equation to the other .

cards.claim: Adding or subtracting the same number on both sides leaves the solution unchanged, but multiplying or dividing both sides preserves it only when the number is non-zero.
cards.quote: The solution of a linear equation is not affected when (i) the same number is added to (subtracted from) both sides of the equation, (ii) both sides of the equation are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero number

cards.claim: NCERT Example 1 solves 2x - 3 = x + 2 by moving 3 to the RHS, subtracting x from both sides, and obtaining x = 5.
cards.quote: Example 1: Solve 2 x – 3 = x + 2 Solution: W e have 2x = x + 2 + 3
cards.equation: 2x - 3 = x + 2 \Rightarrow 2x = x + 5 \Rightarrow 2x - x = x + 5 - x \Rightarrow x = 5

cards.claim: Taking a number away from only one side of an equation is wrong, because the two sides are then no longer equal.
cards.quote: You can’t take 4 from one side and not from the other because then the two sides aren’t equal.

locator.section: Side note: an equation is like a scale
